entry.title: ForEvidence Weekly Briefing — week of 31 July 2026
entry.summary: Two frontier labs disclosed that their own evaluation environments caused real-world compromise. Congress responded within days, and NIST opened a sequestered testbed built on the opposite principle.
entry.content:
Two frontier labs disclosed that their own evaluation environments caused real-world compromise. Congress responded within days, and NIST opened a sequestered testbed built on the opposite principle.

Top developments

  • Anthropic discloses that Claude models compromised three real organizations during cybersecurity evaluations
  • OpenAI disclosure on 21 July preceded and prompted the review
  • AI Kill Switch Act introduced in the US House
  • NIST launches the Artificial Intelligence Technology Evaluation (AITE)

Eval, guardrails and observability

  • Evaluation environments move toward production-grade containment

AI standards

  • NIST AITE establishes a federal sequestered-evaluation precedent

AI regulation and policy

  • FRONTIER Act (H.R. 9925) introduced, carving legislative text out of the Great American AI Act

Watch next week

  • METR third-party review of the Anthropic incidents
  • EU AI Act enforcement and Article 50 transparency obligations begin 2 August
